layers.title: The Root
layers.subtitle: What this Name means linguistically
layers.content:
The Name Ar-Razzaaq (الرَّزَّاق)

The Provider

The Name comes from the root ra-za-qa (ر ز ق), from which rizq — provision, sustenance — is derived. Ar-Razzaaq is the intensive form (fa''aal), meaning the One who provides abundantly, continuously, and to every creature without exception.

This Name is established for Allah in His Book and affirmed among the Most Beautiful Names, as the Prophet said: 'Verily to Allah belongs ninety-nine names, one hundred less one. Whoever enumerates them will enter paradise.' (Sahih Muslim)
layers.quran_ref: Quran 51:58 — 'Indeed, it is Allah who is Ar-Razzaaq (the Provider), the Possessor of strength, the Firm.'
layers.hadith_ref: The Prophet said: Verily to Allah belongs ninety-nine names, one hundred less one. Whoever enumerates them will enter paradise. — Sahih Muslim
layers.source: Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen, Commentary on the 99 Names of Allah

layers.title: The Meaning
layers.subtitle: The full understanding of this Name
layers.content: The Provider — the One who creates all provision and delivers it to every creature He has made. His providing is not occasional but unceasing: He sustains the believer and the disbeliever, the human and the animal, the one who thanks Him and the one who forgets Him. He provides the outward sustenance of the body — food, drink, wealth, health — and the inward sustenance of the heart: knowledge, faith, contentment and guidance. No provision reaches anyone except by His decree, and none can withhold what He has apportioned or grant what He has withheld.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 51:58 — 'Indeed, it is Allah who is Ar-Razzaaq (the Provider), the Possessor of strength, the Firm.'
layers.source: Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen, Commentary on the 99 Names of Allah

layers.title: In the Quran
layers.subtitle: Where Allah calls Himself by this Name
layers.content:
Allah calls Himself Ar-Razzaaq in the Quran. The placement of each Name is not accidental — when Allah closes a verse with a Name, He is signalling that the meaning of that Name is the reason for what preceded it.

Quran 51:58 — 'Indeed, it is Allah who is Ar-Razzaaq (the Provider), the Possessor of strength, the Firm.'

Related verses: 'And there is no creature on earth but that upon Allah is its provision.' (Quran 11:6) — 'Say: Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth?' (Quran 10:31) — 'And Allah provides for whom He wills without account.' (Quran 3:37)

The scholars of tafseer note that knowing which Name closes which verse deepens understanding of the Quran itself. The Name is the key to the verse.

layers.source: Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen, Commentary on the 99 Names of Allah

layers.title: The Scholar
layers.subtitle: Ibn Uthaymeen's explanation
layers.content:
Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen (rahimahullah), one of the foremost scholars of the 20th century, explained the Name Ar-Razzaaq:

The Provider — the One who creates all provision and delivers it to every creature He has made. His providing is not occasional but unceasing: He sustains the believer and the disbeliever, the human and the animal, the one who thanks Him and the one who forgets Him. He provides the outward sustenance of the body — food, drink, wealth, health — and the inward sustenance of the heart: knowledge, faith, contentment and guidance. No provision reaches anyone except by His decree, and none can withhold what He has apportioned or grant what He has withheld.

Ibn Uthaymeen taught that truly knowing the Names of Allah changes a person — not merely memorising them, but understanding their meaning and then living in light of them. He who knows Allah as Ar-Razzaaq will relate to Allah differently, supplicate to Him differently, and trust in Him differently.
layers.source: Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen, Commentary on the 99 Names of Allah

layers.title: Your Reflection
layers.subtitle: What this Name means for your life
layers.content:
The Name Ar-Razzaaq is not only something to know about Allah — it is something to live in relation to.

The Prophet said: 'Verily to Allah belongs ninety-nine names. Whoever enumerates them will enter paradise.' The word for enumerate — ahsaha — means to know, understand, act upon, and call upon Allah by each Name appropriately.

Reflect: When do you most need to call upon Allah as Ar-Razzaaq? What situation in your life right now makes this particular Name the one you need most? The Names of Allah are not a list to memorise — they are doors to knock on in different moments of need.

The Quran says: 'And to Allah belong the best Names, so call upon Him by them.' (7:180)

quiz.prompt: What is the primary meaning of the Name Ar-Razzaaq?

options.text: The Provider
The Restorer
The Reckoner
The Withholder

quiz.citation: Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen, Commentary on the 99 Names
quiz.scholar_reflection: The Name Ar-Razzaaq means: the provider. Understanding the precise meaning allows you to call upon Allah by this Name at the right moment.

quiz.prompt: Which verse of the Quran affirms the Name Ar-Razzaaq for Allah?

options.text: Quran 51:58 — 'Indeed, it is Allah who is Ar-Razzaaq, the Possessor of strength, the Firm'
Quran 2:255 — 'Allah, there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence'
Quran 112:1 — 'Say: He is Allah, the One'
Quran 59:23 — 'He is Allah, the Sovereign, the Pure, the Perfection'

quiz.citation: Quran 51:58 — 'Indeed, it is Allah who is Ar-Razzaaq (the Provider), the Possessor of strength, the Firm.'
quiz.scholar_reflection: Allah affirms this Name for Himself: 'Indeed, it is Allah who is Ar-Razzaaq (the Provider), the Possessor of strength, the Firm.' (Quran 51:58). A Name is established for Allah only by the Quran or the authentic Sunnah — never by human invention.

quiz.prompt: What is the Arabic root that the Name Ar-Razzaaq is derived from?

options.text: Ra-za-qa (ر ز ق) — to provide, to sustain; the source of the word rizq (provision)
Ra-za-na (ر ز ن) — to be weighty or dignified
Ra-ja-a (ر ج ع) — to return or come back
Ra-za-'a (ر ز ع) — to divide into portions

quiz.citation: Classical Arabic lexicography of the Divine Names — Ibn Uthaymeen, Commentary on the 99 Names
quiz.scholar_reflection: The Name comes from the root ra-za-qa (ر ز ق), from which rizq — provision, sustenance — is derived. Ar-Razzaaq is the intensive form (fa''aal), meaning the One who provides abundantly, continuously, and to every creature without exception.

quiz.prompt: According to the hadith, how many Names of Allah are there, and what is promised to the one who enumerates them?

options.text: Ninety-nine — whoever enumerates them will enter Paradise
One hundred — whoever writes them will be forgiven
Ninety-nine — whoever recites them nightly will be granted wealth
Seventy — whoever memorises them will be raised in rank

quiz.scholar_reflection: The Prophet said: 'Verily to Allah belongs ninety-nine names, one hundred less one. Whoever enumerates them will enter paradise.' Scholars explain that enumerating (ihsa') means memorising them, understanding their meanings, worshipping Allah by them, and calling upon Him through them.

quiz.prompt: What does the Quran command believers to do with the Most Beautiful Names of Allah?

options.text: Call upon Him by them
Recite them only in Ramadan
Write them on the walls of the masjid
Keep them hidden from the general people

quiz.citation: Quran 7:180 — 'And to Allah belong the best Names, so call upon Him by them'
quiz.scholar_reflection: The Names were revealed to be used. Allah does not merely inform us of them — He commands us to call upon Him by them, which means matching the Name to the need in the moment of du'a.

quiz.prompt: Allah is Ar-Razzaaq — the provider. When in your life have you most needed Him to be this for you?
quiz.slider_label: How often do you call upon Allah by this specific Name?

options.text: In a moment of fear or danger
When I needed something no one else could provide
When I felt ashamed or broken
I have not thought about needing this quality specifically

quiz.scholar_reflection: The Names of Allah become real to us in the moments we need them most. Each Name is a door — Allah placed exactly this Name in your path at exactly this moment.

quiz.prompt: If you truly believed Allah is Ar-Razzaaq at every moment, what would change first in how you live?
quiz.slider_label: How much does this Name currently shape your daily choices?

options.text: How I speak when no one is listening
What I chase and what I let go of
How much anxiety I carry about the future
How I treat people who cannot benefit me

quiz.scholar_reflection: Ibn Uthaymeen taught that knowledge of a Name is incomplete until it changes conduct. The test of knowing a Name is not what you can recite about it, but what you do differently because of it.

quiz.prompt: Which obstacle most keeps you from living with awareness that Allah is Ar-Razzaaq?
quiz.slider_label: How present is this awareness in an ordinary day?

options.text: Distraction — I simply forget
Doubt — I know it intellectually but do not feel it
Habit — my routines were built without it
Impatience — I want to see it proven on my timeline

quiz.scholar_reflection: Naming the obstacle honestly is the beginning of removing it. The Quran repeatedly links forgetfulness of Allah to the corrosion of the heart — awareness is a practice, not a mood.

quiz.prompt: How would you explain the Name Ar-Razzaaq to someone who has never heard of it?
quiz.slider_label: How confident are you in your understanding of this Name?

options.text: Through a story from my own life
Through the verse of the Quran that affirms it
Through what it means about Allah's perfection
I could not yet explain it clearly

quiz.scholar_reflection: Being able to teach a Name simply is a sign you have understood it. If you cannot yet explain it, that is not failure — it marks exactly where your study should continue.

quiz.prompt: What du'a will you make tonight, calling on Allah specifically as Ar-Razzaaq?
quiz.slider_label: How specific are your du'as usually?

options.text: For something I have been afraid to ask for
For someone else who needs it more than me
For steadiness rather than for change
For forgiveness before anything else

quiz.citation: Quran 7:180 — 'And to Allah belong the best Names, so call upon Him by them'
quiz.scholar_reflection: This is the final step of ihsa' — moving the Name from the mind to the tongue in supplication. A du'a that names the attribute you are relying on is a du'a that knows who it is addressing.
